title: Engine Miles
tagline: An iPhone app that estimates the split between electric miles versus gas-engine miles for your plug-in hybrid
summary: Engine Miles is an iPhone app made for plug-in hybrids. You log your fill-ups, and it estimates how many of your miles were on the gas engine, so you can track oil changes by engine miles instead of the odometer. Regular hybrids work too. It's been on the App Store since October 2026.

overview.what: An iPhone app for plug-in hybrid owners. You log your fill-ups, and it estimates how many of your miles were electric and how many were on the gas engine. It works for regular hybrids too, just without the electric split.
overview.why: My dad keeps a paper logbook for his plug-in hybrid to work out how many miles are on the gas engine, because the car doesn't really tell you. I wanted to turn his notebook into an app.
overview.did: I designed and built it in Swift and SwiftUI, using AI as a coding tool. Everything stays on your phone, with no account and no server, and my dad tested every build.
overview.result: It's been live on the App Store since October 2026, with a free version and Engine Miles Pro. Now I'm working on getting it in front of more plug-in hybrid owners.

sections.heading: Why I built it
body: My dad bought a 2022 RAV4 Prime, which is a plug-in hybrid. Since the day he got it, he's kept a paper logbook to work out how many of his miles were electric and how many were on the gas engine, because the car doesn't really tell you. The odometer counts every mile, but a lot of those miles never touch the engine, and that matters for things like oil changes.
So I wanted to turn his notebook into an app. Something quick enough to use at the pump, that does the math for you.

media.alt: Engine Miles home screen with an estimated 17,837 engine miles, about 59% electric over the car's lifetime, an oil change due in about 1,911 engine miles, the last fill-up and the odometer
media.caption: The home screen, with example data.

sections.heading: How it works
body: Every time you fill up, you type in the gallons, and the app multiplies them by your car's gas-only MPG. That's an estimate of how far the engine went on that tank, and adding up the tanks gives you engine miles. It's an estimate, not a reading from the car. There's no car connection at all, and your owner's manual still has the final say on maintenance.
The oil change tracker counts down on those engine miles instead of the odometer. Once a month the app also asks you for an odometer check-in, which keeps the estimate on track.

media.alt: Engine Miles oil change screen with 1,911 estimated engine miles to go, around late December, a goal of 5,000 miles or 12 months, and a history of past oil changes
media.caption: The oil change countdown.

sections.heading: Building it with my dad
body: I built it in Swift and SwiftUI, and everything stays on your phone. There's no account and no server, so your log never leaves your iPhone. The free version covers one car, unlimited fill-ups, the estimate, the oil countdown and the monthly check-in. Pro adds insights, reminders and more cars for $1.99 a month, $9.99 a year or $29.99 once.

My dad tested every build on TestFlight before it went out, and he's a great tester because he says exactly what he thinks. One screen used to say "whole car", and he asked what that was even supposed to mean, so now it says "car's lifetime".

media.alt: Engine Miles log screen listing fill-ups and month-end odometer check-ins by month, with the estimated engine miles for each month
media.caption: Fill-ups and month-end check-ins, by month.

media.alt: Engine Miles Insights screen with a 2026 year recap, about 69% electric this year split into electric and estimated engine miles, and Fuel and MPG and Money cards
media.caption: Insights, part of Pro.

sections.heading: Where it's at
body: Engine Miles went live on the App Store in October 2026. It's still early, so right now I'm mostly working on getting it in front of more plug-in hybrid owners. There's a lot more I want to add, and my dad keeps finding things for the list.
